# An exact third-mass obstruction at the true mixed centroid

The true mixed centroid of an equal-endpoint three-fiber family is an
actual point of its middle fiber. Nevertheless its raw halfspace depth
need not be one third of the total mass, even for planar fibers and
middle mass between one and three. This note gives an exact rational
actual-body certificate and a one-parameter first-moment mechanism.
It does not refute the weaker hollow-edge target, nor OC.

Subsequent theorem: the weaker edge target at this same true mixed
centroid is now proved for arbitrary equal-volume endpoints and every
d>=1 in `candidate 660db01ed45063dd`.
Thus the exact third-mass obstruction below bounds a stronger constant;
it is not a remaining obstruction to that edge theorem.

## 1. Rational convex bodies and the exact true centroid

Set

    k=1725/577, c=91/345, l=22/345,
    K={(x,y):0<=x<=1, |y|<=k(1-x)},
    A=B=K intersect {l<=x<=c}.

The triangle K has area k. Its vertical section length is 2k(1-x),
so its ordinary centroid is (1/3,0). Both endpoint trapezoids have
area one, because

    |A|=k[(1-l)^2-(1-c)^2]
       =(1725/577)[(323/345)^2-(254/345)^2]=1.

Their common x-coordinate of centroid is their first moment

    mu_A=k[(c^2-l^2)-(2/3)(c^3-l^3)]=31807/199065.

Put these fibers at bases -1,0,1 and form their convex hull C. Since
A=B is contained in K, its endpoint midpoint is contained in K;
therefore C has exactly these three integer fibers. The body C is
compact and convex and has nonempty ambient interior. Its mixed mass is

    M=k+2=2879/577.

The equal endpoint masses make its true mixed base centroid zero.
Reflection in y=0 makes the second continuous centroid coordinate zero,
and the first continuous coordinate is

    (k/3+2mu_A)/(k+2)=91/345=c.

Consequently Y=(0,c,0) is the true mixed centroid and belongs to S.

## 2. The exact cap certificate

The closed ambient halfspace H={x>=c} contains Y. Its endpoint traces
are supporting line segments; they are nonempty but have zero area.
Its middle trace is the similar apex triangle of area

    P=k(1-c)^2=64516/39813.

Thus

    depth_S(Y)<=P/M=64516/198651<1/3,
    M/3-P=567/13271>0.                                  (1)

This refutes a proposed third-of-total-mass guarantee at that specified
center. In contrast,

    P-(k+1)/3=11570/39813>0.

The displayed cap does not refute the weaker planar hollow-edge target
(k+1)/3. Nor is this a best-center obstruction: the endpoints are equal
copies, so the independently proved paired-centroid theorem gives an
actual center with raw depth at least 4/3, sufficient for that target
when k<=3. No lower bound or exact depth at Y is inferred from its one
explicit upper certificate.

## 3. The generating moment identity and its normalized cap curve

For h>0 put

    a=(2+4h^3)/(3-6h^2), b=a+h,
    k=1/(b^2-a^2), c=1-a, l=1-b.                        (2)

Whenever 0<a<b<=1 and 1<=k<=3, use the same K and endpoint slices as
in Section1. Their area is one. Their first moment below c has the exact
deficit

    c-mu_A=(2k/3)(b^3-a^3)-a.

The true-centroid condition c=(k/3+2mu_A)/(k+2) is therefore equivalent to

    (k+2)a-2k/3=(4k/3)(b^3-a^3).

Substitution of k=1/(b^2-a^2) and b=a+h reduces this to
3a-2-6ah^2-4h^3=0, exactly the choice in(2). Hence these are actual
centroid certificates, not freely specified first moments. Their
displayed cap has normalized mass

    rho(h)=k a^2/(k+2)
      =4(2h^3+1)^2/[3(1-2h^2)(4h^4+8h+3)],
    k(h)=3(1-2h^2)/[h(2h^3+3h+4)].                     (3)

The rational instance in Sections1–2 is h=1/5.

There is a precise interval describing this branch. Let h_0 be the
unique root in(19/100,1/5) of 2h^4+5h^2+4h-1=0, and h_* the unique
root in(23/100,7/30) of

    2h^3-6h^2-3h+1=0.                                  (4)

Uniqueness on these intervals follows from strict monotonicity of the
displayed polynomials, and their endpoint signs are rational checks.
For h in[h_0,h_*], (2) is feasible, k decreases from three to
1/(2h_*-h_*^2)>1, and b increases to one. In particular the support
endpoints remain actual points of the triangle. One can verify these
claims directly from (2), using h_*<1/4: a'>0, hence b'>0, and

    k'(h)=6(2h^2+1)(2h^3-3h-2)
             /[h^2(2h^3+3h+4)^2]<0.

The normalized displayed-cap value has derivative

    rho'(h)=16(2h^3+1)(2h^3-3h-2)(2h^3-6h^2-3h+1)
       /[3(2h^2-1)^2(4h^4+8h+3)^2].                    (5)

It is strictly negative before h_* and zero at h_*. Thus the minimum
of this particular cap curve on this feasible branch occurs at h_*,
where b=1 and

    rho(h_*)=(1-h_*)^2/(1+4h_*-2h_*^2).

This is a exact algebraic cap upper certificate. It is not asserted to
be the minimum depth of this family over every direction, nor the
optimal normalized centroid depth over arbitrary compatible triples.
The rational certificate(1) already suffices to reject the third-mass
proposal without relying on any approximation to h_*.

## 4. Scope of the fixed-knot linear formulation

The associated directional problem has an exact finite linear model.
For fixed support intervals and fixed knots, let f,g,h denote concave
nonnegative section-length profiles of the two endpoints and middle.
Require integrals of f,g equal one, the integral of h lie in[1,3], and
the combined first moment integral of s(f+g+h) equal zero. Require
at every pair of endpoint profile vertices that the middle profile at
their averaged abscissa be at least half their summed heights. Because
the middle hypograph is convex, these finitely many inequalities are
exactly inclusion of the entire Minkowski midpoint of the two symmetric
profile bodies. They are linear in the heights when the knots are fixed.

All averaged endpoint abscissae are required to lie in the prescribed
middle support interval, including zero-height support endpoints.
The positive-halfline integral of f+g+h is also linear in those heights.
Every feasible vector thus realizes an actual convex-compatible triple
with true mixed centroid zero and exactly that cap mass. Conversely
every symmetric profile triple with those knots satisfies the model.
This finite formulation does not justify varying supports or reducing
arbitrary profiles to a fixed number of knots. The analytic family
above supplies the obstruction independently of numerical optimization.
